the DWO instability is a global instability that is characterized by a strong dependence on the inlet conditions.
DWO and Ledingg instability are analyzed for boiling in a single tube, and for condensing in a single tube with sub-cooled, over-heated, and saturated inlet conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the stability of boiling and condensing single-phase systems.
the development of a numerical method for the analysis of two-phase flow instabilities in boiling and condensing single tube systems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DWO are not a problem in condensing systems, whereas Ledinegg instability can occur in condensing and in particular in boiling systems.
Ledinegg instability is a more general instability than DWO.
DWO and Ledinegg are not a major problem in condensing systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model for the analysis of two-phase flow instabilities and have applied the model to the analysis of boiling and condensing instabilities.
the numerical model is capable of predicting DWO and Ledinegg phenomena in a single tube boiling and condensing system.
the numerical model is capable to predict the stability limits with high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability limits of DWO and Ledinegg instability in boiling and condensing are similar.
the Ledinegg instability is not only present in boiling but also condensing systems.
Ledinegg instability is more severe than DWO and that the Ledinegg instability is more likely to occur in condensing systems than boiling systems.
